1. ABOUT JHS
JHS is a full-service Chartered Accountant firm established in 1981, headquartered in Mumbai with 13 offices across India. We
have 500+ team members serving 600+ clients across Assurance, Taxation, Consulting, and Outsourcing.
Our Vision
To be a globally respected premier assurance and accounting firm, most preferred in every location we serve.
Our Values
We are focused on instilling our values in our people and processes to create sustainable growth and provide uncompromised
quality to our clients.

2. JOINING & ONBOARDING
Induction
Every new joiner goes through a structured induction covering:
● HR Induction — Company overview, policies, culture, and values
● IT Induction — Systems, tools, and access setup
● Technical Induction — Role-specific skills and audit techniques
● A Welcome Kit is provided to all new joiners after BGV.
Background Verification (BGV)
HR conducts a thorough background check on all new joiners including credentials, residence, and experience verification.
Article Trainee Registration
As per ICAI guidelines, Article Trainees will be registered on their official date of joining. All required documents must be
submitted in advance.
Joining Form
Entry-level new joiners are required to sign an undertaking form during onboarding covering commitment to the role,
organizational discipline, and protection of training investment.

3. OFFICE HOURS & ATTENDANCE
Office Hours
● Saturdays are generally non-working days, but may be required for submitting for Deliverables/Special Projects.
● Training on holidays/Saturdays does not count as a working day or entitle Comp Off.
● Attendance is mandatory for all training invitees.
Late Mark Policy
● Grace period for JHS Staff: 30 minutes (late after 10:00 AM)
● Grace period for Article Trainees: 45 minutes (late after 11:15 AM)
Attendance Rules
● JHS Staff must complete minimum 9 hours/day to be marked Present
● Article Trainees must complete minimum 7.5 hours/day
● Punching IN/OUT from home is not allowed unless approved by Partner/TL
● If punch-out is not marked, it will be treated as Half Day
● Attendance regularization is allowed maximum 5 times per payroll cycle (21st–20th)
● Lunch break: 30 minutes, after 1:00 PM
● HR conducts surprise attendance checks between 9:30 AM – 11:00 AM
● Shortfall in work hours will result in financial deductions
📌
Payroll is processed on the basis of HRMS-recorded attendance only. Once the calendar is locked, no changes will be accepted.

4. TIMESHEET
A Timesheet defines what each employee is expected to track and report. It is evaluated monthly and directly impacts appraisals
and payroll. Every employee must submit a monthly Timesheet to maintain accountability and transparency. It captures project-
wise time allocation, achievements, and areas for improvement.
Timesheet Evaluation Points
● Timely completion of assignments
● Quality and Excellence of work
● Audit Documentation
● Learning & Development participation
● Buddy/Business referrals
● Work ethic and attitude
● MIS report submissions
What to Include
● Number of actual days worked during the month
● Project-wise breakdown of time spent on each client
● Hits (achievements) — e.g., zero missed punches, client appreciation, Hall of Fame participation
● Misses (areas to improve) — e.g., missed KRAs, punctuality issues, task delays
● Idle time — system issues, waiting for client data, transitions between projects
Submission Process
● HR shares a Google Form link at the end of every payroll cycle
● Form covers the period from 21st of previous month to 20th of current month
● Last date to submit: 22nd of every month by 12:00 PM
● Late submissions will not be accepted
● Non-submission will result in salary being withheld for that month
● TLs and Managers must ensure all team members (including new joiners completing 1 month) submit on time
📌
Select the correct form based on your designation. Submitting the wrong form will be treated as non-compliance.

5. WORK FROM HOME POLICY
JHS strongly promotes working from office or client location. Work from Home (WFH) is an exception, not a standard practice.
Key Rules
● WFH requires prior approval from Client, CHRO, and Partner
● An official WFH email request must be submitted
● Email must be sent to Partner and TL with CC to HR
● WFH without approval will lead to disciplinary action including salary deduction or termination (if repeated multiple
times)
● WFH is approval-based and limited. Performance and availability will be monitored.

6. PAY DAY & CONVEYANCE
Payroll Cycle
● Payroll cycle: 21st of the month to 20th of the following month
● Salary is processed on the last working day of the month
● Salary shall be credited in compliance with applicable statutory timelines.
● Accounts team will inform 1 day in advance if there is any delay
● Employees on Professional Service Basis must submit their Invoice and approved Timesheet on or before 22nd of every
month
Conveyance
● Conveyance cycle: 21st to 20th (same as payroll cycle)
● Conveyance is paid by the 15th of every month
● Claims with original attachments must be submitted to the payroll team by the 24th
● No claims are accepted after the 24th
Annual Leave — JHS Staff & Retainers
● 18 days of Paid Leave per year (April to March cycle)
● Confirmed staff: 1.5 days accrued per month
● Probation staff: 1 day accrued per month
● Maximum 12 leaves carried forward to next year — must be used by 30th June or they lapse

12. PREVENTION OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT (POSH)
JHS is committed to providing a safe, respectful, and inclusive workplace free from sexual harassment.
Sexual harassment shall be defined in line with applicable law and includes any unwelcome physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct
of a sexual nature.
The workplace includes office premises, client locations, virtual work environments, and any work-related interactions.
Interim relief measures may be provided during the pendency of inquiry as per applicable law.
Internal Committee (IC)
IC members shall serve a defined tenure and the committee composition may be reviewed periodically to ensure balanced
representation.
How to File a Complaint
● Submit a written complaint (physical or email) on posh@jhsassociates.in to the IC within 3 months of the incident
(extendable by IC as per law)
● Include details of the incident, date, time, and any witnesses
Redressal Process
● Complaint acknowledged within 7 working days
● Formal inquiry completed within 90 days
● Employer must act on IC recommendations within 60 days
● Either party can appeal within 90 days of the recommendation
● All proceedings are kept strictly confidential
Key Protections
● No retaliation against complainants or witnesses — any reprisal leads to disciplinary action
● False or malicious complaints are also a serious offense
● POSH awareness sessions conducted annually
● IC members receive specialized training
📌
Ethics Helpline: 809 709 5057 | Email: posh@jhsassociates.in

13. DISCIPLINARY BANDS POLICY
JHS follows a color-coded progressive disciplinary system to ensure fairness and consistency.
Anti-Harassment Policy
Harassment includes physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct that causes offence, discomfort, or embarrassment. Any JHS staff
aware of such conduct must immediately inform HR. Violations are subject to disciplinary action up to termination.
Employee Grievance Policy
JHS encourages all employees to raise workplace concerns in a timely and transparent manner. All grievances will be handled
confidentially and without any retaliation.
Reporting Channels:
• HR Helpdesk (primary mode – auto-ticket based)
• Email: hr@jhsassociates.in
• Ethics Helpline: 809 709 5057
• Written communication to HR / Management
Resolution Process & Timelines:
• Acknowledgement: Immediate (auto-generated via HR Helpdesk)
• Review: Within 24 working hours
• Action Initiation: Within 3–5 working days (depending on complexity)
• Final Resolution: Within a maximum of 7 working days
Virtual Chai pe Charcha:
HR will conduct a monthly open forum / virtual connect where employees can openly share feedback, concerns, or suggestions
directly with the CHRO in an informal and approachable setting.
This initiative is aimed at encouraging open communication, improving workplace experience, and enabling timely resolution of
employee concerns.
Whistle Blower Policy
JHS encourages staff to report suspected misconduct without fear of punishment. Reports can be made via:
● Email: hr@jhsassociates.in
● Post: Attention Mr. Huzeifa Unwala, 406 B Wing, Navkar Chambers, Marol Naka, Andheri East, Mumbai – 400059
● Ethics Helpline: 809 709 5057

JHS collects and processes employee personal data for legitimate business purposes including recruitment, onboarding, payroll,
attendance, and compliance.
All personal data shall be handled in accordance with applicable data protection laws, including the Digital Personal Data
Protection Act, 2023.
The Company ensures that:
• Data is collected with appropriate consent and for defined purposes
• Access to personal data is restricted to authorized personnel only
• Reasonable safeguards are in place to protect data from unauthorized access, loss, or misuse
Employees are expected to maintain confidentiality of all internal and client data and must not share or misuse such information.
Workplace Health, Safety & Wellbeing
JHS is committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment for all employees.
Key provisions include:
• Employees working late hours may be provided appropriate safety support as required
• Women employees working beyond standard hours will be supported with necessary safety measures
• Annual health check-ups may be conducted for employees above 40 years of age
• Any workplace hazards, incidents, or safety concerns must be immediately reported to HR/Admin
All employees are expected to adhere to safety guidelines and contribute to maintaining a secure workplace.

15. LOAN / ADVANCE POLICY
Eligibility
● Only confirmed JHS staff who have completed 1 year of employment
● Loan can be availed for children's education, medical expenses, or hospitalization of a family member
Loan Terms
● Maximum amount: 2x monthly take-home salary, up to Rs. 1 Lakh
● Interest free
● Repayment: within 6 months; EMI starts from the immediate next month
● Re-application allowed only after 12 months from the previous loan
● Loan amount will be adjusted in Full & Final Settlement if employee exits

16. SEPARATION POLICY
Notice Period
● Employees who cannot serve full notice must pay CTC equivalent for shortfall days.
● No leave can be taken during notice period — medical leave requires a doctor's certificate
● Leave taken during notice period extends the notice period/ will be adjusted against the F&F
● F&F will be processed subject to completion of all exit formalities including submission of all company assets (hardware
and software)
● F&F will be processed within 2 working days subject to completion of all exit formalities and the employee approving
the F&F
● Notice period will not be shortened
Reasons for Termination
● Three consecutive negative performance evaluations
● Fund embezzlement, misuse of office property
● Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information
● Breach of JHS or client code of conduct
● Transfer of client data to personal devices
● Intoxication on official premises or during official business
● Non-performance of duties or gross negligence
● Client complaint or Code of Conduct violation leads to immediate termination
● Serious misconduct
● 2+ Yellow Band warnings
Exit Process
● Complete handover of responsibilities
● Obtain clearance certificate
● Attend exit interview with HR on last working day
● Return all firm property: laptop, SIM card, ID card, access cards, files, diskettes (assets)
● Email ID to be remapped or deleted with due approvals
Full & Final Settlement
● Non-gratuity staff: F&F processed within 2 working days subject to completion of all exit formalities and the employee
approving the F&F
● Gratuity staff: F&F processed within 2 working days subject to completion of all exit formalities and the employee
approving the F&F
● Timesheet and OPE must be submitted on last working day, failing to do so will mean deduction in F&F
